## Goal

First-party plugins prove every contract, including the license flow for non-OSI engines.

## Owned requirements

Close each with the check below, through the real public interface (README §3).

| ID | Requirement | Route | Concrete check |
|---|---|---|---|
| EX-05 | First-party plugins prove the contracts (xterm.js engine, MCP App exporter, Remotion adapter, GSAP adapter) | I, B | Each first-party plugin passes `mostra plugin verify` against its baselines |

## Scope

From [WORK_PACKAGES.md](../WORK_PACKAGES.md):

the Remotion adapter and the GSAP adapter (user-installed, with the license flow), the chart datum anchor provider (from WP-20, packaged), the filesystem connector and `mostra term record`; and the contract proofs for every first-party plugin, including the WP-17 exporter and the WP-23 engine.

Design detail for this package:

- Remotion and GSAP adapters (user-installed, `--accept-license`), chart datum anchor provider, filesystem connector, `mostra term record`.
- `mostra plugin verify` against each plugin's baselines.

## Out of scope

- The registry (v1.x)

Plus the files every WP reads ([README.md](README.md) §1).

## Acceptance evidence

each plugin passes its baselines through `mostra plugin verify`; the license audit shows no non-OSI code in the core bundle; the license acknowledgment is recorded in the lockfile.

Also: `pnpm check` green, diff reviewed, the progress report's evidence table complete for every owned requirement (README §3), the evidence matrix regenerated, docs and AGENTS.md current, and the report finalized after acceptance (README §4).

## Risks and notes

- Never add Remotion or GSAP to any core dependency tree; the license audit enforces it.
